{{Short description|Non-linear equation in fluid dynamics}}
[[File:Exploring High-Resolution Sea Surface Height Data from NASA’s SWOT Satellite (SVS5538 - 8k 05820).jpg|thumb|300x300px|Satellite view of internal solitary waves in the [[Andaman Sea]] off the coast of Thailand. Dubreil-Jacotin–Long equation describes their motion.]]
In [[fluid mechanics]], the '''Dubreil-Jacotin–Long''' ('''DJL''') '''equation''' is one of the main [[nonlinear partial differential equation]] used to describe [[gravity waves]] (waves in water). This equation is equivalent to [[Euler equations (fluid dynamics)|Euler equations of fluid dynamics]] for stratified media.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Stastna |first=Marek |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Internal_Waves_in_the_Ocean/HNh1EAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=djl+equation&pg=PA66&printsec=frontcover |title=Internal Waves in the Ocean: Theory and Practice |date=2022-06-16 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-3-030-99210-1 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Du |first=Peng |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Internal_Wave_Hydrodynamics_on_Submersib/xH6lEQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22DJL+equation%22+gravity+waves&pg=PA22&printsec=frontcover |title=Internal Wave Hydrodynamics on Submersibles: Volume 1: Interactions Between Internal Waves and Structures |last2=Wang |first2=Chao |last3=Zhao |first3=Sen |last4=Wen |first4=Jun |last5=Xie |first5=Luo |last6=Hu |first6=Haibao |date=2026-01-01 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-981-95-4479-0 |language=en}}</ref> It describes the motion of [[Internal wave|internal waves]] as [[Soliton|solitons]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Encyclopedia_of_Ocean_Sciences/z2-SDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=djl+equation&pg=RA2-PA539&printsec=frontcover |title=Encyclopedia of Ocean Sciences |date=2019-04-12 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-813082-7 |language=en}}</ref>

The equation was first proposed by [[Marie-Louise Dubreil-Jacotin]] in 1932<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dubreil-Jacotin |first=M.-L |date=1932 |title=Sur les ondes de type permanent dans les liquides hétérogenes |journal=Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei Rendiconti |language=fr |volume=6 |pages=814–819}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dubreil-Jacotin |first=M.-L. |date=1937 |title=Sur les théorèmes d'existence relatifs aux ondes permanentes périodiques à deux dimensions dans les liquides hétérogènes |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=JMPA_1937_9_16_1-4_43_0 |journal=Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées |language=fr |volume=16 |issue=1-4 |pages=43–67 |issn=1776-3371}}</ref> and was popularized by Robert R. Long in 1953.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Long |first=Robert R. |date=1953-01-01 |title=Some Aspects of the Flow of Stratified Fluids: I. A Theoretical Investigation |url=https://doi.org/10.3402/tellusa.v5i1.8563 |journal=Tellus |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=42–58 |doi=10.3402/tellusa.v5i1.8563 |issn=0040-2826|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Description ==
The DJL equation assumes a two-dimensional [[Inviscid flow|inviscid]], [[Incompressible flow|incompressible]], [[Potential flow|irrotational]] flow under the action of [[surface gravity]] described under [[Boussinesq approximation (water waves)|Boussinesq approximation]].<ref name=":0" /> The simplest DJL equation for a fixed frame without background flow is given by<ref name=":0" /><math display="block">\nabla^2 \eta +\frac{N(z-\eta)}{c^2}\eta = 0,</math>where <math display="inline">c</math> is the unknown wave propagation speed, <math display="inline">z</math> is the vertical coordinate, and <math display="inline">\eta(x,z)</math> denotes the vertical ([[isopycnal]]) displacement, where <math display="inline">x</math> is the horizontal coordinate and <math display="inline">N^2</math> is the [[Brunt–Väisälä frequency]] (buoyancy frequency), given by<math display="block">N^2(z)=-g\frac{\mathrm d \bar{\rho}(z)}{\mathrm d z},</math>where  <math display="inline">g</math> is the [[gravitational acceleration]] and <math display="inline">\bar\rho(z)</math> is the average density. Boundary conditions are such that <math display="inline">\eta(x,0)=\eta(x,-H)=0</math> and <math display="inline">\eta(|x|\to \infty)\to 0</math>, where <math display="inline">H</math> is the total water depth.

Solving the DJL equation allows to obtain <math display="inline">\eta(x,z)</math> and <math display="inline">c</math>. The DJL equation is a nonlinear [[elliptic partial differential equation]]. It is an eigenvalue problem where <math display="inline">c</math> is the eigenvalue for the solution <math display="inline">\eta(x,z)</math>.<ref name=":2" />

DJL equation is useful for the description of internal solitary waves. The DJL equation describes waves of permanent form and cannot describe their formation. Rigid-lid approximation is necessary to avoid coexisting small-amplitude waves with the same <math display="inline">c</math> which carry energy into or away. For their formation, the [[Korteweg–De Vries equation]] is often used.<ref name=":2" /> 

By using the relation <math display="inline">\varphi=\eta c</math> one can derive the [[Flow velocity|flow velocity field]], where <math display="inline">\varphi</math> is the [[stream function]].<ref name=":0" />

== Equation with background flow ==
If a steady background current of speed <math display="inline">U(x,z)</math> is present, the full DJL equation becomes<ref name=":2" /><math display="block">\nabla^2 \eta - \frac{U'(z-\eta)}{U(z-\eta)-c}[\eta_x^2+(\eta_z-2)\eta_z] +\frac{N(z-\eta)}{(U(z-\eta)-c)^2}\eta = 0,</math>where <math display="inline">\eta_x,\eta_z</math> are the horizontal and vertical derivatives of <math display="inline">\eta</math>.
